name: rungs
title: L0, L1, L2: one page, three ways to deliver it
html:
L0, L1, L2: one page, three ways to deliver it

Like a page with its CSS and JavaScript inlined, or linked and cached.

L0

State, forms and schemas in one answer

Simple and correct: like a page with everything inlined.

L1

Prefer: forms=link

The form set is its own content-addressed link, cached.

L2

Prefer: forms=link, schema=link

Schemas linked too: immutable, shared across forms, states and resources.

“L0 buys correctness, L2 buys economy.” HTTP caching does the scaling, as it always has on the Web.

Bytes: JSON bodies before compression, headers excluded. Extrapolated from the measured warm release.
say: The analogy: a web page with all its CSS and JavaScript inlined, versus the same page with linked, cached files. Same page, different delivery. L0 inlines everything; L1 links the form set; L2 links the schemas too, content-addressed and immutable for a year. The numbers are from five real releases per forge, with no model calls. From the second release on, about 50 form-set and schema reads per release never reach the network: ARTIE's cache answers them. Resources themselves still revalidate by ETag and answer 304. That's a mock-up. Now two real services that agree on nothing.
